title: Cross-category experience is recalled
given: An experience item is tagged to multiple taxonomy nodes (cross-category) and committed.
when: recall is run with a taxonomyNodeId filter matching any one of the item's categories
then: The item appears in the candidates because tag membership links it to multiple categories without copying canonical content.
notes: Maps to packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts (recall) which exercises taxonomy branch selection and FTS recall.

title: A misclassified record remains discoverable through FTS
given: An item is committed with a wrong or arbitrary taxonomyNodeIds classification but correct title and summary text.
when: recall is run with text matching the item content and no taxonomy filter
then: The FTS index finds the item by text even though its taxonomy classification is wrong.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts ("an item misclassified in taxonomy is still found via FTS text match").

title: Semantically equivalent wording retrieves the same experience
given: An experience was saved with one wording and an embedding provider is configured.
when: recall is run with semantically equivalent but lexically different wording
then: The same experience is retrieved via embedding cosine similarity, not only exact FTS matches.
notes: Rubric: Does a paraphrased query retrieve the same item that an exact query retrieved, when an embedding provider is configured? Requires a live embedding model.

title: Refuted memory never enters positive recommendation ranking
given: An item has its status set to "refuted" (or "superseded").
when: recall is run at fast or standard tier (which include only "active" statuses)
then: The refuted item is excluded from candidates and never appears in a positive recommendation ranking.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts ("deep-tier recall includes superseded/refuted items, standard does not") and packages/memory-core/src/retrieval-plan.test.ts (planRetrieval includeStatuses).

title: Material preference use is disclosed
given: A stored user preference materially changes a recommendation during a consultation.
when: The consultant produces the answer using recall results that include that preference
then: The answer discloses which preference or experience materially shaped the result via memoriesUsedDisclosure.
notes: Rubric: Does the final answer explicitly disclose the preference or experience that materially shaped it? The disclosure channel (memoriesUsedDisclosure) is deterministic, but the agent's disclosure behavior needs a live model.

title: Progressive disclosure stays within its token budget
given: A recall query targets a tier with a token budget (fast 300, standard 1200, deep 3000).
when: recall runs and estimateTokens accumulates the injected memory
then: The returned usedTokens does not exceed the tier budget and truncated is set when content is cut off.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-core/src/retrieval-plan.test.ts (planRetrieval, estimateTokens) and packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts ("recall honors planRetrieval caps").

title: Repeated session saves do not duplicate experience
given: The same host session is saved multiple times, including a package update with a new title.
when: commit is called repeatedly with previewTokens from prepare
then: There remains one SessionExperience and one item per topicKey, with no duplicate ranking candidates; replays with the same previewToken return created=false.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts ("commit is idempotent" and "commit upserts the session package and items with no duplicate ranking candidates on repeated saves").

title: Sensitive fields remain absent without confirmation
given: A prepared item includes sensitiveFields with confirmed=false.
then: commit rejects with SENSITIVE_UNCONFIRMED naming each unconfirmed field, and no sensitive content is persisted.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts ("unconfirmed sensitiveFields are rejected with SENSITIVE_UNCONFIRMED naming each field").

title: Forget removes canonical and derived content
given: An item with derived summaries, embeddings, tags, and FTS rows has been committed.
when: memory_manage forget is called for that item
then: Canonical rows, derived summaries, embeddings, tag memberships, and FTS rows are all removed, and subsequent recall returns nothing for that item.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts ("forget removes canonical rows + derived + FTS rows and subsequent recall returns nothing").

title: Indexes rebuild after model changes
given: The embedding or summarization model is changed and derived indexes are stale.
when: the janus-memory CLI reindex command is run
then: The FTS index (and derived embeddings) are dropped and rebuilt from canonical tables without losing accepted experience.

title: Interrupted enrichment does not damage canonical records
given: A commit completes its canonical transaction but the deferred derived enrichment (summary or embedding) is interrupted.
when: the store is reopened and recall is run
then: The canonical experience item and its decision remain intact and retrievable; only the derived artifact is missing and retryable.
notes: Maps to packages/memory-sqlite/src/store.test.ts (commit transaction) which proves canonical writes complete in one transaction before deferred enrichment. The retryable-derived contract is part of the store design.

title: Concurrent processes share one database without corruption
given: Several processes (for example one OpenCode window each) open the store on the same directories at the same instant, including the first-time migration.
when: each commits its own session plus one session shared by all of them and recalls memory
then: Every open and commit succeeds, no session or item is lost or orphaned, the integrity and foreign-key checks pass, and migrations apply exactly once.
notes: Covered by packages/memory-sqlite/src/multi-instance.test.ts (multi-process stress test) and migrations.test.ts (failed migration rolls back).
